boundary.words: All right, cool. I think the boundary makes sense here. Let's go to the next stage.

overview.words: This mission seems roughly correct. I still want to get into the weeds about how the exact onboarding works, but as long as we understand this is about: how we intake players, how we get them through onboarding, what happens after they onboard, what's the gate to go and manage the team. I think we're good. So, as long as we think that's handled, I'm good to continue.

boundary_amendment.words: Part of the inflow port flow should do the check for them to see who the people are that are there... This collection loop has to deal with the player roster onboarding... This is just for players.
boundary_amendment.change: Three doors named, not one: the recruit flip, the import, and adding by hand. The recruit's answers and this-season consent carry into onboarding and their open link is superseded. The import follows the event-import shape with a preview page and a potential-duplicates section. Leaving mid-onboarding stops the ask and leaves records alone. Onboarding's own chase-and-flag surface is retained, extending Mission 6's. The collection loop is players only; coaches and committee leave entirely for their own missions.

inventory.words: Okay, I like that. ... The workflows look fine, except that I want to see what the actual questions in inventario are.

workflows.name: A flipped recruit lands in onboarding
Say yes and fill in your details
Fix something the club has wrong
Pick up a chase that ran out

Which class an item carries is per-season configuration, not code.

areas.name: The import door
areas.belongs: Portfolio row 7 names CSV import and carry-forward as how existing players arrive, and Mission 5's intake routed it here.

areas.name: The far side of the recruit flip

areas.name: The import inherits the roster's season
areas.belongs: Every membership must belong to a season, and Brian settled on 2026-09-01 that the import never chooses or creates one.
areas.invariant: An import always writes into the season the roster is currently in. It never asks which season and never creates one.
areas.reason: A rule binding W1 and W2 rather than a journey of its own; season creation is a later mission's.

areas.name: Duplicate check before anything is created
areas.belongs: Importing a squad against existing people manufactures duplicate humans unless the check is in front of the operator.
areas.reason: Brian, 2026-09-01: a page showing who is about to be added with potential duplicates listed underneath. Mission 5's duplicate machinery is reused, not rebuilt.

areas.name: Import failure and partial rows
areas.belongs: A file an operator produced from a spreadsheet is hostile by default; rows will fail.
areas.reason: Rows that fail are explained without losing the ones that worked, following the event import's confirmation shape.

areas.name: The welcome message
areas.belongs: Task 10 §8 trigger 1 and Task 07's single message-class exception; the one message the club may send to obtain agreement.

areas.name: The compiled ask, one open per person ever

areas.reason: New facts join the open ask rather than starting a second; nobody receives parallel nag threads.

areas.name: The form's adaptive content

areas.name: The recruit's answers carried in
